name: bubble-sq
comment: SQUARE BUBBLE TILES (Chase, Field & McCluer, 'Puzzle Pieces and Bubble Tiles', working draft 2026-08-22). Sibling of bubble-tri: same complementary matching rule (a bump must meet a bite), square substrate instead of triangular. The six tiles are the binary necklaces of length 4 (OEIS A000031), the paper's S0/S1/S2A/S2B/S3/S4. Unlike the triangular family the BITE COUNT is no longer the tile's identity: two bites splits into S2A (adjacent, edges IIBB) and S2B (opposite, IBIB), which is why the shelf keys tiles on the canonical rotation of the whole bite word. B = bump, I = bIte, both unit length. Angles in D=24 units: 90 = 6, four to a vertex, so maxValence 4 is exact and not a bound. All six tiles are achiral (each necklace's reverse is one of its own rotations), so no mirror twins appear. The SEARCH needs EU_EDGE_COMPL=1 and the developer --complement.
